record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.original_question: Fix k ∈ N. In every coloring of the edges of the hypercube Q_n with k + 1 colors, must there exist a geodesic path between two antipodal vertices that uses at most k color changes?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8.4. Let k ∈ N. In any k + 1-colouring of the edges of Qn, there exists a geodesic path between two antipodal vertices, with at most k colour-changes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q_n$ denote the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph, whose vertex set is $\{0,1\}^n$ and whose edges connect pairs of vertices differing in exactly one coordinate. Two vertices $u,v \in \{0,1\}^n$ are called antipodal if they differ in every coordinate. A geodesic between two antipodal vertices is a path of length $n$ (equivalently, a shortest path) joining them. Given an edge-coloring of $Q_n$ and a path $P = e_1 e_2 \cdots e_n$ in $Q_n$, the number of color changes along $P$ is the number of indices $1 \le i \le n-1$ such that $e_i$ and $e_{i+1}$ receive different colors.

Fix $k \in \mathbb{N}$. Prove or disprove: for every $n \ge 1$ and every edge-coloring of $Q_n$ using $k+1$ colors, there exist antipodal vertices $u, v \in \{0,1\}^n$ and a geodesic from $u$ to $v$ along which the number of color changes is at most $k$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a generalization of the Feder–Subi conjecture (the case k=1, restricted to paths rather than geodesics) and related to the Leader–Long conjecture. The k=1 geodesic version and the general k ≥ 1 case appear to remain open; only small-dimensional cases of related conjectures have been verified, most recently via SAT solvers (Frankston–Scheinerman, etc.). No proof of the general statement was found in the literature.

status_evidence.snippet: Recent work verifies related antipodal-coloring conjectures only for small n via SAT solvers.
status_evidence.claim: Related conjectures (Feder–Subi, Leader–Long, Norine) remain open in general, with only small-n cases verified.
